question: Should Microsoft Teams adopt `channels.msteams.accounts` and `defaultAccount` as its permanent multi-bot configuration model, including inherited root settings and account-scoped credentials and persisted state?
rationale: The implementation is credible, but it creates compatibility-sensitive configuration, setup, credential, routing, and state contracts that automation cannot approve as permanent product behavior.

options.title: Sponsor the hybrid account model
options.body: Adopt the standard account-based shape while retaining root-level single-bot configuration as the supported compatibility path.

options.title: Request a narrower phased change
options.body: Accept the capability direction but require schema, runtime routing, and state/auth scoping to land in smaller separately reviewed stages.

options.title: Defer multi-bot support
options.body: Keep Microsoft Teams single-account until maintainers are ready to own the added configuration and upgrade surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the hybrid account model
recommendation.body: Adopt the standard account-based shape while retaining root-level single-bot configuration as the supported compatibility path.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing candidate from direct PR engagement and adjacent Teams lifecycle ownership.
